 Little fanfare, plenty of chaos ahead of SAFF Championship
 Published : 5 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 5 November 2026, 13:27
 • 
 FOOTBALL
 SHARE 
 Samsul Arefin Khan
 Samsul Arefin Khan 
 Bhutan team in training. Photo: Facebook 
 The build-up to the 15th edition of the SAFF Championship has been marred by chaos, with a series of organisational shortcomings, including high ticket prices, logistical complications and a lack of promotional activities, raising questions about the tournament's preparations. 
 Even Bangladesh Football Federation (BFF) president Tabith Awal has expressed dissatisfaction with the preparations. Despite Bangladesh being the hosts, the South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) has sold the tournament's commercial rights to TSA Sports and Entertainment, a relatively unknown Bangladesh-based event management company, which is overseeing the arrangements.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 The company is responsible for organising the tournament, promotional activities, team accommodation and travel, as well as fixing and distributing ticket prices. The BFF, meanwhile, has distanced itself from the organisational shortcomings, saying its role is limited to providing logistical support to the organisers. The competition is set to get underway today.
 Image 
 High ticket prices, low fan interest 
 Since Hamza Choudhury began representing Bangladesh, there has been a fresh wave of enthusiasm among football fans, with stadium attendances increasing significantly in recent years.
 However, the announcement of a minimum ticket price of Tk 1,000 for SAFF Championship matches sparked widespread criticism. Ticket sales appeared to justify those concerns, with most tickets remaining unsold a day before the opening day's fixtures, which feature the high-profile India-Pakistan clash followed by Bangladesh's match against Bhutan.
 Less than 24 hours before the opening match, organisers announced a 50 per cent discount on tickets for 100 students for the first day of the tournament. However, the move did little to address broader concerns over ticket prices and fan engagement.
 Little tournament branding or promotion 
 Although Bangladesh are hosting the tournament for the first time since 2018, there has been little visible excitement surrounding the event.
 Both the BFF and SAFF have come under scrutiny for failing to promote the competition adequately. There have been virtually no banners or festoons across the capital to build awareness, while preparations at the venue continued until the eve of the tournament.
 Read more SAFF Championship 2026: All you need to know 
 Uncertainty over teams' arrivals, Sri Lanka's airport ordeal 
 For a considerable period, the media remained in the dark about the arrival schedules of the five visiting teams.
 Bhutan were the first to arrive on November 2, followed by India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka the next day. The Maldives were the last team to reach Bangladesh, arriving just a day before the tournament began.
 Sri Lanka, meanwhile, reportedly had to wait for more than three hours at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka following logistical and coordination problems upon their arrival.
 Bhutan's players also took nearly two hours to complete their visa-on-arrival formalities at the airport.

 Image 
 Pakistan team yet to get their luggage a day before their opening match. Photo: Facebook 
 Pakistan's preparations disrupted before India clash 
 Although Pakistan arrived in Bangladesh on November 3, they could not hold a training session after their team luggage and training equipment were left behind at Hamad International Airport in Doha, Qatar.
 As things stand, Pakistan will face arch-rivals India without having completed a training session in Bangladesh, an unfortunate setback ahead of one of the tournament's most anticipated fixtures.
 No trophy unveiling before the tournament 
 It is customary for tournament organisers to unveil the trophy before a competition gets underway. However, despite an official press conference being held at a city hotel on Wednesday, there was no sign of the SAFF Championship trophy.
 The absence of representatives from the Maldives, who were yet to arrive in the country, was another notable feature of the press conference.
 Image 
 The pre-tournament press meet was held but no sign of the trophy yet. Photo: BFF 
 Bangladesh yet to announce final squad 
 On the eve of the tournament, hosts Bangladesh were yet to announce their final 23-member squad.
 The team initially named a 28-member preliminary squad, but Ronan Sullivan was subsequently ruled out through injury. Isa Foysal also left the camp after being informed that he would not make the final squad.
 Uncertainty over opening ceremony 
 Bangladeshi-origin American DJ and music producer Sanjoy Deb, popularly known as Sanjoy, is scheduled to perform at the opening ceremony of the SAFF Championship. A social media announcement also revealed that the ceremony would begin at 6:00pm.
 However, no details have been provided about its duration, invited guests or the segments planned for the occasion, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the tournament's opening festivities.
